title: Pre-trial sensorimotor EEG complexity does not predict motor-imagery class beyond standard mu/beta ERD (eegmmidbg)
abstract: Test of whether the complexity of the sensorimotor cortex EEG in the rest immediately preceding a motor-imagery trial predicts the trial's class (T1 = left hand vs T2 = right hand) better than the standard mu/beta event-related desynchronization (ERD). Datasets: the public eegmmidbg (BCI2000) — local set subjects S001-S004 (6 files, 90 MI trials) and an independent set subjects S005-S008 (16 files, 240 MI trials), both downloaded from PhysioNet and byte-verified. Features per trial: standard - mu/beta ERD (7.5-12.5 / 15.5-25.5 Hz) during the MI trial vs the preceding rest; novel - sample entropy and permutation entropy (m = 3) of the pre-trial rest, sensorimotor ROI. Outcome: trial class (T1/T2). Evaluation: Mann-Whitney AUCs with bootstrap 95% CIs, 5-fold stratified balanced-accuracy LDA on standardized features, label-shuffle falsification, and cross-dataset transfer (LDA trained on local, tested on independent). Results: local AUCs - erd_mu 0.474, erd_beta 0.605, ent_samp 0.527, ent_perm 0.465; LDA CV - standard 0.545 (novel 0.504). Independent AUCs - 0.427, 0.462, 0.502, 0.494; LDA CV - standard 0.503 (novel 0.429). The local beta ERD AUC of 0.605 (AUC SE ~ 0.06) did not replicate on the independent subjects (AUC 0.462). Conclusion: the proposed pre-trial complexity pattern does not predict motor-imagery class beyond the standard measures in this scope (details and sensitivity in README.md).
